countries.name: Belgium
countries.law: NIS 2 Act of 26 April 2024 + Royal Decree of 9 June 2024
countries.fwName: CyFun 2025 (CyberFundamentals, NIST CSF 2.0-based)
countries.summary: Transposed on time; CyFun 2025 framework; first ex-ante EE checks under way since April 2026.

authorities.name: CCB
authorities.role: Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium - national authority, CyFun certification, incident handling

authorities.name: NCCN
authorities.role: National Crisis Centre - national cyber crisis management plan (with CCB)

fw: CyFun framework with three assurance levels (Small ≈25, Basic ≈50, Important ≈75 measures), complemented by NIST CSF, ISO 27001/27002, IEC 62443 and CIS Controls references.
CyFun 2025 (published 1 Oct 2025, NIST CSF 2.0 + governance category) will be the only accepted version after the transition period.
Presumption of conformity via the CyFun Conformity Assessment Scheme (CAS) or ISO/IEC 27001 (SoA submitted by 18 Apr 2026, certificate by 18 Apr 2027).
reg: Registration on atwork.safeonweb.be was due by 18 Mar 2025 (5 months after entry into force).
Any change to company information must be notified within 2 weeks.
inc: Significant incidents reported to the CCB within 24h, full report within 1 month, via the dedicated platform (guide published by the CCB).
Notification must include detailed description, severity/impact, root cause, mitigation measures and cross-border impact.
aud: EE: mandatory regular conformity assessment; first control 18 Apr 2026 (18 months after entry into force), then annual checks for EE and IE.
Ex-ante inspections possible for EE at any time; federal public sector assessed by the Federal Internal Audit Service.
scope: Sector list can be extended by royal decree; CER-designated critical entities are automatically EE.
Local authorities not systematically included (case-by-case designation as 'strategic entity' by the CCB); public administration entities exempt from administrative fines.
other: Financial entities under DORA are exempt from the security rules but must still register with the CCB and notify significant incidents.
reco: Register with the CCB, choose CyFun vs ISO 27001 (Wavestone recommends CyFun unless ISO 27001 already in place), run gap analysis and remediation plan before the April 2026/2027 milestones.

timeline.text: NIS 2 Act voted in plenary (published 17 May 2024)
Law enters into force - on time
CyFun 2025 published (NIST CSF 2.0 base, governance category added)
CER law adopted; designated critical entities become NIS 2 EE automatically
Compliance deadline passed; CCB inspection service starts ex-ante verification of EE

next: By 18 Apr 2027: end of CyFun transition period; general compliance progress report due.

countries.name: Croatia
countries.law: Cybersecurity Act NN 14/2024 + Cybersecurity Regulation NN 135/2024
countries.fwName: National framework - 13 themes, 145 controls (ISO 27001/2 & NIST 800-53 aligned)
countries.summary: Transposed on time; authority-driven categorisation; 145-control framework with 3 criticality levels.

authorities.name: NCSC-HR
authorities.role: National Cybersecurity Centre (within SOA) - central authority

authorities.name: ZSIS
authorities.role: Information Systems Security Bureau - certification schemes, auditor accreditation

authorities.name: CARNET / ZSIS CSIRTs
authorities.role: Sectoral CSIRTs (banking, digital infrastructure / energy, transport, health, public admin)

fw: 13 main themes, catalogue of 145 controls aligned with ISO 27001/2 and NIST 800-53; measures apply per criticality level (basic / medium / advanced) assigned by national risk assessment.
Sub-measures tagged A (mandatory), B (conditional), C (recommended); all measures cover both IT and OT.
Compliance required within 1 year of receiving the categorisation notification.
reg: Entities do not self-register: competent authorities identify and notify each entity (spring 2025 wave).
Requested data must be transmitted within 15 days of categorisation; lists verified every 2 years.
inc: Significant incidents notified to the competent CERT via forms on the PiXi platform (CARNET).
Beneficiaries must be informed within 72h; note: the Croatian law does not replicate the 24h early-warning explicitly.
aud: EE: cybersecurity audit at least every 2 years by accredited auditors (ISO 27001, CyFun, KRITIS certifications recognised); conclusions to authorities within 8 days, costs borne by entities.
IE: self-assessment at least every 2 years; audit only on authority request.
scope: Any entity supplying a service/good of major societal or economic importance can be designated regardless of size; e-invoicing exchange platforms are EE; public communication network providers are IE.
Education entities can be IE regardless of size; special physical-security measures for digital infrastructure entities.
other: DORA provisions integrated (third-party ICT provider definitions); CER directive not referenced.

timeline.text: Cybersecurity Act (NN 14/2024) enters into force - on time
Cybersecurity Regulation (NN 135/2024) in force: classification criteria, risk measures, incident notification
NCSC-HR: initial categorisation under way; entities notified by mid-April 2025
ZSIS publishes self-assessment guidelines (control calculator, risk framework, 145-control catalogue)
Public consultation on certification rules for cybersecurity audits closed

next: During 2026: additional implementing regulations and new National Cyber Security Strategy expected.

countries.name: Czechia
countries.law: Cybersecurity Act No. 264/2025 Coll. + implementing decrees of 14 Oct 2025
countries.fwName: Tiered regime - higher obligations: 14 org. themes (169 measures) + 11 technical (127); lower: 13 themes (81 measures)
countries.summary: In force Nov 2025 (12-month delay); strictest requirement count in the panel (296 EE measures); 6h early warning.

authorities.name: NÚKIB
authorities.role: National Cyber and Information Security Agency - supervision, dedicated portal

authorities.name: National CERT
authorities.role: Incident response for the lower-obligations regime

fw: Two regimes: higher obligations (≈EE, ISMS explicitly required) and lower obligations (≈IE).
OT/industrial control systems: dedicated technical measures (§27).
Entities have 12 months from registration to implement measures; 'strategically important services' carry extra supply-chain obligations.
reg: Registration with NÚKIB within 60 days of the law entering into force (by 31 Dec 2025); asset inventory (primary + supporting) must be declared, exclusions justified.
Provider report within 30 days of registration decision; later changes notified within 90 days.
inc: Early warning within 6 hours (24h for trust service providers) - stricter than the directive.
Incidents lasting over 1 month: supplementary reports every 15 days until the final report; reactive counter-measures ordered by the authority must be applied within 72h.
aud: EE: annual security audits (first required from 1 Nov 2026); other entities every 2 years; independent auditors.
Cybersecurity audit at least every 2 years and on significant change (§16).
scope: Defence industry sector added; sub-sectors added: gas stations, electricity suppliers for data centres, in-flight refuelling, qualified e-ID systems, payment/e-money institutions, research infrastructure.
Regulator can designate critical exceptions; criticality criteria quantified in decree No. 408/2025.
reco: Inventory primary and supporting assets required for the regulated service before registration.

timeline.text: Senate approves the bill; signed by the President 26 June 2025
Act No. 264/2025 Coll. published in the Collection of Laws
Two implementing decrees published (essential / important entities)
Law and decrees enter into force
Registration deadline (60 days) for regulated services

next: First audits required for essential entities from 1 Nov 2026.

countries.name: Germany
countries.law: NIS-2 Implementation Act (published 5 Dec 2025) + KRITIS-Dachgesetz (17 Mar 2026, CER)
countries.fwName: No single national standard - sector regulations + recognised standards (ISO 27001, BSI 200-3/200-4, B3S, KRITIS)
countries.summary: In force Dec 2025; ~29,500 entities in scope, enforcement phase running - unregistered entities face fines up to €500k after 31 July 2026.

authorities.name: BSI
authorities.role: Federal Office for Information Security - supervision, registration, incident notification

authorities.name: BBK
authorities.role: Federal Office for Civil Protection and Disaster Assistance

fw: No dedicated NIS 2 standard: entities follow stricter sector regulation where it exists (e.g. DORA, EnWG for energy), otherwise choose recognised standards (ISO 27001, BSI 200-3/200-4, sectoral B3S, KRITIS).
Compliance required by 6 Dec 2028; proof of compliance renewed every 3 years.
Two entity categories: critical facilities (KRITIS + essential) and important facilities.
reg: Registration due 6 Mar 2026 (or within 3 months of qualifying); ≈38.5% of ~29,500 entities registered at the deadline; BSI in active control phase since May 2026.
Unregistered entities asked to regularise by 31 Jul 2026, fines up to €500,000; registered data must be updated annually.
Digital-infrastructure and KRITIS entities provide extra data (public IP ranges, critical ICT services).
inc: Incidents reported to the BSI since the notification channel opened on 6 Jan 2026; standard NIS 2 deadlines; interim reports on BSI request.
aud: KRITIS operators transmit audit/certification results and identified vulnerabilities to the BSI; remediation plans can be required.
Independent audits/inspections can be ordered ex-ante for essential entities, ex-post for others; proof requests possible at the earliest 3 years after the law.
scope: Public sector = federal administration entities only; municipalities and non-federal administrations not automatically in scope; defence/interior exempt (reporting duties remain).
Health: major labs, R&D, medical facilities under NIS2+KRITIS; finance under DORA; space = ground infrastructure.
other: DORA-regulated entities exempt from NIS 2; KRITIS framework recognised; seven-tier penalty scale up to €10M/2% (EE) and €7M/1.4% (IE), €500k tier for registration failures.
reco: Executive members must complete cybersecurity risk training as soon as possible, then every 3 years; identify applicable standards or select a framework.

timeline.text: Bundestag adopts the NIS 2 transposition law
Law published in the Federal Gazette; in force 6 Dec 2025
BSI opens registration platform and incident notification form
Registration deadline - ≈38.5% of in-scope entities registered
KRITIS-Dachgesetz (physical resilience / CER) enters into force
BSI enters active enforcement phase; regularisation demanded by 31 July 2026

next: By 6 Dec 2028: all registered entities fully compliant; proofs renewed every 3 years.

countries.name: Greece
countries.law: Law 5160/2024 + Ministerial Decision 1689/2025 (national framework)
countries.fwName: National framework - 22 mandatory cybersecurity controls (Decision 1689/2025)
countries.summary: Law in force Nov 2024; 22-control national framework since May 2025; 2026-2030 national strategy adopted.

authorities.name: NCSA
authorities.role: National Cybersecurity Authority (cyber.gov.gr) - sole regulator and central contact point

authorities.name: National CSIRT
authorities.role: Incident management (EYP/NIS CERT for central government and municipalities)

authorities.name: ADAE
authorities.role: Contact point for electronic communications, with reinforced sectoral powers

fw: 22 mandatory controls covering technical, organisational and operational aspects; no explicit reliance on an international standard.
Since 6 May 2025 the national framework is the mandatory reference for NCSA audits and inspections.
Local-specificity highlights: mandatory internal AND external penetration testing at least annually (or after major incident).
reg: Registration on the NCSA digital platform; final deadline extended to 30 Sep 2025.
Changes notified within 2 weeks (3 months for some digital providers); detailed data set incl. domain names; strict identification of 'critical' entities without size thresholds.
inc: Online form on the NCSA portal + email; obligation applicable since entry into force.
Definition includes 'moral harm' and a preventive approach (notifiable as soon as an incident is 'likely' to have serious impact); NCSA can tighten criteria by decision.
aud: On-site and off-site inspections incl. spot checks; special audits after incidents, complaints or serious indications; supervision of EE and IE security evaluation.
Appointment of an ICT Security Officer (Υ.Α.Σ.Π.Ε.) mandatory - role incompatible with DPO; full asset inventory classified by criticality required.
scope: Special regimes: electronic communications (ADAE), energy incl. EV charging operators and hydrogen, space ground infrastructure, health manufacturing, MSP/MSSP essential regardless of size.
Local authorities in scope since 27 Nov 2025; central government reports incidents to the National CERT (EYP/NIS).
other: DORA is lex specialis for finance; NCSA coordination mechanism with sector regulators still maturing.

timeline.text: Law 5160/2024 enters into force
Ministerial Decision 1689/2025: national framework of 22 controls published
Extended registration deadline for data submission to the NCSA
Law applies to local authorities (regions and municipalities)
National Cybersecurity Strategy 2026-2030 adopted

next: Alignment with the 2026-2030 strategy: EL-SOC connection, future Cyber Hotline for incident support.

countries.name: Hungary
countries.law: Cybersecurity Act LXIX of 2024 + implementing decrees (Jan 2025)
countries.fwName: Three security classes - Basic / Significant / High: 120 / 200 / 280 measures
countries.incidentMethod: Report to Special Service for National Security
countries.summary: In force Jan 2025; classification of IS in 3 security classes; audit deadline extended to 30 June 2026; supervision fee regime.

authorities.name: SZTFH / SARA
authorities.role: National transposition and supervision authority

authorities.name: NKI
authorities.role: Defence cybersecurity authority

authorities.name: KNBSZ
authorities.role: CERT and certification authority (intelligence services)

authorities.name: Special Service for National Security
authorities.role: National cybersecurity incident management centre

fw: EE must classify information systems into Basic / Significant / High classes; IE must at least meet the Basic class within 1 year.
Data hosted on public cloud or abroad must be classified by confidentiality, integrity, availability.
Compliance demonstrated using ICT services/products/processes certified under a European or national scheme; 2 years granted to EE for security measures.
reg: Registration via form SZTFH 420 within 30 days; authority reviews and issues a decision; updates within 15 days.
Annual supervision fee payable to the SZTFH (decree 2/2025).
inc: Incidents reported to the Special Service for National Security; incident management plan mandatory; beneficiaries informed within 72h.
Sectoral variations: reporting requirements can differ by sector and competent incident centre.
aud: Contract with an SZTFH-approved audit body was due by 31 Aug 2025; first audit by 30 Jun 2026 (extension approved 2 Oct 2025).
Classification and security policy reviewed at least every 2 years; failed audits trigger a remediation plan within 90 days.
scope: Cement/lime/gypsum production added to Manufacturing; electronic communications services added as highly critical.
Banking and financial market infrastructure excluded (DORA); public administration sector not listed; public transport sub-sector added.
other: Law implements NIS 2 and CER, referencing ENISA and DORA regulations.
reco: Run the IS risk analysis to determine the security class; contract an approved auditor; start data classification (Basic/Significant/High).

timeline.text: Cybersecurity Act LXIX in force (government + ministerial decrees Jan 2025)
SZTFH decrees on audit procedure and supervision fees published
Law XXIII in force; supervision fees due
Audit deadlines extended: auditor contract 31 Aug 2025, first audit 30 Jun 2026

next: Several clarifying regulations still expected.

countries.name: Italy
countries.law: Legislative Decree 138/2024 + ACN Decision No. 164179 (10 Apr 2025)
countries.fwName: NIST CSF 2.0-based framework - EE: 43 measures / 116 req.; IE: 37 measures / 87 req.
countries.summary: Transposed on time; NIST CSF 2.0 framework; incident notification binding since 15 Jan 2026; measures due by 1 Oct 2026.

authorities.name: ACN
authorities.role: Agenzia per la Cybersicurezza Nazionale - national authority

authorities.name: Sector ministries
authorities.role: Sectoral authorities per NIS 2 sector

authorities.name: CSIRT Italia
authorities.role: National CSIRT - incident notifications

fw: Framework built on the 6 NIST CSF 2.0 functions (GV, ID, PR, DE, RS, RC); measures in annexes 1-2 of Decision 164179.
EE-only additions: periodic vulnerability/penetration testing, secure baseline configurations, secure hardware decommissioning, inbound traffic filtering incl. email.
Implementation of security measures due by 1 Oct 2026 (18 months after ACN validation).
reg: Registration on the ACN portal 1 Dec 2024 - 28 Feb 2025 (17 Jan for digital providers); ACN validation notified 15 Apr 2025 triggering all deadlines; annual updates (activities, NIS contact + substitute).
Data includes Codice Fiscale, security officers, public IPs/domains, EU member states served; changes within 14 days.
inc: Notification to CSIRT Italia via form, binding since 15 Jan 2026 (9 months after registration).
Trigger criteria IS-1 to IS-4 (confidentiality, integrity, service levels, unauthorised access) - IS-4 applies to EE only.
aud: ACN may review documentation, run on-site/remote inspections incl. random checks; regular or ad-hoc audits after major incidents.
Self-assessments mandatory for EE and IE; first one from 16 Oct 2026 (no frequency set yet).
scope: Public administration broadly covered: constitutional bodies, ministries, tax agencies, independent authorities; via annex, all local/regional authorities and publicly controlled bodies.

timeline.text: Legislative Decree 138/2024 in force - on time
ACN decisions 164179 (framework), 136117 (portal), 136118 (info-sharing) published
NIS Guidelines (basic technical specifications) published
Annual information update + substitute contact designation completed
Incident notification to CSIRT Italia becomes enforceable

next: By 1 Oct 2026: security measures of the 2025 Italian framework fully implemented.

countries.name: Latvia
countries.law: National Cybersecurity Law (in force 1 Sep 2024) + Regulation No. 397 + Minimum Cybersecurity Requirements (2 Jul 2025)
countries.fwName: Minimum Cybersecurity Requirements - 94 measures, Class A/B/C system
countries.incidentMethod: Email forms 1-5 (24h) to national security service
countries.summary: Transposed on time; 94-measure framework scaled by A/B/C classes; cybersecurity manager with citizenship rules for critical ICT.

authorities.name: NCSC (Ministry of Defence)
authorities.role: National Cybersecurity Centre - policy and supervision

authorities.name: SAB
authorities.role: Constitution Protection Bureau - critical ICT oversight

authorities.name: CERT.LV
authorities.role: Incident response, prevention, SOC supervision

authorities.name: MilCERT
authorities.role: Defence-sector incident response

fw: Requirements scaled by confidentiality/integrity/availability class (A/B/C): prescriptive log retention (18/12/6 months, NTP Stratum 2+ timestamps), MFA rules, encryption baselines.
Cybersecurity manager to be appointed (vetted; Latvian citizen for critical ICT infrastructure); first self-assessment report was due 1 Oct 2025.
Cybersecurity policy reviewed and communicated to the authority every 3 years; single national Internet traffic bridge for State-linked EE/IE.
reg: Self-assessment test by 1 Apr 2025 then registration form (annex 10) via official e-address; extra notification for critical ICT owners; changes within 2 weeks.
inc: Incidents reported within 24h to the specialised national security service via staged forms (early warning → final report); reporting live since 1 Jul 2025.
Vulnerabilities: report to the authority within 5 days; remediation 90 days (180 if technically impossible).
aud: NCSC can run or order compliance audits on suspicion of violations; independent certified auditors (ISO 27001, CISSP, CISA, CISM; ≥2 years experience), costs borne by the entity.
Annual self-assessment for the most critical classes, every 3 years otherwise.
scope: EE: institutions directly/indirectly linked to the State, sole providers of a service in Latvia, EU reference labs; IE: mid-size security/education/trust service providers.
Outsourcing restricted by country/ownership with prior authority opinion; official register of authorised auditors.

timeline.text: National Cybersecurity Law in force - on time
Regulation No. 397 on minimum cybersecurity requirements in force
'Minimum Cybersecurity Requirements' regulation approved (94 measures)
Deadline: cybersecurity manager appointed + first self-assessment report

next: Additional sectoral regulatory texts expected.

countries.name: Lithuania
countries.law: Cybersecurity Law No. XII-1428 + government resolution of 12 Nov 2024
countries.fwName: Description of cybersecurity requirements - 12 themes (ISO 27001-based)
countries.summary: Transposed on time; NKSC registered entities by Apr 2025; 12-theme ISO-based framework; audits every 3 years.

authorities.name: NKSC
authorities.role: National Cyber Security Centre - supervision, registry, technical assistance

fw: 12 main themes combining specific requirements (policies, training, business continuity) and technical requirements (network security, encryption); grounded in ISO/IEC 27001.
Organisational requirements within 12 months of registry entry, technical measures within 24 months.
Local specificities: availability thresholds >96%/99% for critical IS; mandatory ISP contracts with response times and DoS protection (incl. 24/7).
reg: NKSC selected and registered entities in the KSIS registry by 17 Apr 2025 (authority-driven); entities could contest their categorisation.
Self-check questionnaire available from the Ministry of Defence; after confirmation, entities connect to KSIS and provide activity data.
inc: Notifications to the NKSC per the National Cyber Incident Management Plan via the dedicated platform; quantified thresholds (operational, financial, third-party damage, physical security).
aud: Independent cybersecurity audit at least every 3 years; targeted audits at entity's cost when high risk detected; audits max 4 months (+2 extension).
Sectoral and NKSC-led audits start officially in 2027; first ex-post EE compliance assessments due 1 Jan 2029.
scope: Universities and research institutions added; scientific research for commercial purposes explicitly included.
Public administration (central, regional, municipal) classified EE - subject to corrective orders and public naming instead of fines.
other: Explicit links to DORA, eIDAS, GDPR.
reco: Managers: cybersecurity training every 2 years, documented; vulnerability disclosure embargo 90 days; NKSC can deploy sensors on EE networks.

timeline.text: Cybersecurity Law No. XII-1428 in force - on time
Government resolution amending the 2018 implementation text in force
NKSC completes initial registry of cybersecurity entities (KSIS)

next: 2027: sectoral and NKSC audits begin; 1 Jan 2029: first ex-post EE compliance assessments.

countries.name: Malta
countries.law: Legal Notice 71 of 2025 (+ Legal Notice 22 of 2026 - full entry into force)
countries.fwName: Belgian CyFun adopted as national framework (Dec 2025)
countries.summary: Law Apr 2025; joined the CyFun Scheme Owner Group and adopted the Belgian framework; fully applicable since 23 Jan 2026.

authorities.name: MHSE
authorities.role: Ministry for Home Affairs, Security and Employment

authorities.name: CIPD
authorities.role: Critical Infrastructure Protection Department - national supervisory authority

authorities.name: CSIRTMalta
authorities.role: National CSIRT - incident notifications, coordinated vulnerability disclosure

fw: Malta officially adopted the Belgian CyFun framework (ISO 27001, IEC 62443, NIST CSF, CIS Controls based) after joining the CyberFundamentals Scheme Owner Group on 12 Dec 2025.
reg: National self-registration mechanism maintained by the CIPD; registry reviewed at least every 2 years; changes notified within 3 months.
inc: Incident notifications submitted to CSIRTMalta; National Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure Policy (NCVDP) in place, CSIRTMalta acting as trusted intermediary.
aud: CIPD powers: on-site inspections, audits, security scans, information requests, data access; sector regulators (MCA for ICT, MFSA for finance) also supervise.
Entities must appoint a qualified auditor approved by the authority (valid international/EU certification or background check).
scope: Public administration incl. central government and, after risk assessment, regional entities; national security/defence/law-enforcement excluded.
Criminal Code (Computer Misuse) being revised to align vulnerability-reporting frameworks.

timeline.text: Legal Notice 71 of 2025 transposes NIS 2
Malta joins the CyberFundamentals Scheme Owner Group - Belgian CyFun adopted
Full entry into force of all provisions (Legal Notice 22 of 2026)

next: Practical implementation depends on upcoming CIPD decisions on registration modalities and requirements.

countries.name: Portugal
countries.law: Regime Jurídico da Cibersegurança - Decreto-Lei 125/2025 + Regulamento 756/2026
countries.fwName: QNRCS v2 - 6 objectives, 117 measures, 3 levels (Básico/Substancial/Elevado)
countries.summary: RJC in force Apr 2026 (~18-month delay); QNRCS v2 framework final since 22 June 2026; compliance deadline 22 June 2028.

authorities.name: CNCS
authorities.role: Centro Nacional de Cibersegurança - national authority (sector authorities may supplement)

fw: QNRCS v2 adopted as national framework: 6 objectives (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover), 117 measures; levels Básico/Substancial/Elevado for private entities, groups A/B for public.
Based on NIST CSF 2.0, ISO 27001 and CIS CSC v8.1; voluntary certification via EC QNRCS, ISO/IEC 27001 or DNP TS 4577-1 (Selo Digital) gives presumption of conformity.
Compliance deadline: 22 June 2028.
reg: Registration on MyCiber within 60 days of go-live (before 22 Aug 2026) or within 30 days of gaining EE/IE status; provisional then definitive registry with 10-working-day hearing.
Data: name, tax ID, sector, entity type, addresses, EU member states served, headcount, turnover; cybersecurity officer + permanent 24/7 contact point designated via the platform.
inc: Notifications via MyCiber forms in three stages (initial, end-of-significant-impact, final/interim); email or phone fallback; NIS 2 deadlines.
Significant-incident definition per Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690 where applicable; CNCS technical instruction pending for the rest.
aud: EE: ex-ante supervision (on-site/remote inspections, regular or targeted audits, random checks); IE: ex-post on evidence of non-compliance; targeted audit costs borne by the entity.
scope: 'Relevant public entities' - Portuguese specificity: Group A (≥250 staff, obligations close to IE) and Group B (75-249 staff, lighter obligations).
other: Law 46/2018 and Decree-Law 65/2021 repealed; DORA entities notify ICT incidents to DORA authorities but keep RJC officer/contact-point duties.

timeline.text: Decreto-Lei 125/2025 published - transposes NIS 2
RJC enters into force (~18 months after the EU deadline)
Regulamento 756/2026 published; QNRCS v2 becomes the national framework - regime fully operational

next: Registration on MyCiber before 22 Aug 2026; two CNCS technical instructions pending (significant-incident definition, certification equivalence matrix); compliance by 22 Jun 2028.

countries.name: Slovakia
countries.fwName: 19-theme national framework (decree 227/2025), incl. OT measures
countries.summary: In force Jan 2025; JISKB platform for registration and incidents; 19-theme framework with explicit 3-2-1 backup rule.

authorities.name: NBÚ
authorities.role: National Security Authority - supervision (with sector ministries)

authorities.name: SK-CERT
authorities.role: National Cybersecurity Centre - 24/7 incident management, coordinated disclosure

fw: Decree 227/2025 sets minimum measures across 19 themes: governance, risk, supply chain, IAM, cryptography (annual robustness reassessment), OT safeguards, business continuity.
Local specificities: explicit 3-2-1 backup rule; incident definition includes averted threats and identified vulnerabilities.
Scope of measures determined by risk analysis (annex 1 of decree 226/2025); security documentation kept current for NBÚ inspection.
reg: Registration via JISKB within 60 days of starting activity; law applicable 30 days after registry entry; NBÚ online classification wizard available.
Entities without EU seat must appoint a representative in Slovakia (cloud, DNS); changes notified within 14 days.
inc: Significant incidents reported via JISKB since 1 Jan 2025; criteria in annex I of decree 226/2025; annexes II-III define report content.
aud: EE: mandatory certified audits, first within 2 years of registration; IE: self-assessment via JISKB, certified audit within 5 years.
NIS 1 entities: 2024 audit deadline extended to 30 Sep 2025, previous audit obligations usable until Dec 2026; full compliance for already-registered entities by 31 Dec 2026.
scope: Thermal energy sub-sector added; water & atmosphere sector (drinking/waste water, meteorology, hydraulic structures); nuclear energy follows the law in addition to Atomic Act 541/2004.
Public administration: 3 ministries as competent authorities; large municipalities and regions included if disruption impacts public order/health; public entities face corrective orders, not fines.
other: NBÚ can temporarily suspend executives on repeated failures (private sector); state of cyber crisis can be declared.

timeline.text: Amendment to Act 69/2018 (Act 366/2024) in force
Decrees 226/2025 (incidents) and 227/2025 (minimum requirements) in force
Extended audit deadline for former NIS 1 entities

next: Full compliance of registered entities by 31 Dec 2026.

countries.name: Slovenia
countries.law: Information Security Act ZInfV-1 (adopted 23 May 2025, emergency procedure)
countries.fwName: Law-defined measures (art. 21-22) referencing EU/international standards - no dedicated framework planned
countries.summary: ZInfV-1 in force June 2025; self-registration closed Dec 2025; risk measures due Dec 2026 (Jun 2026 for ex-NIS1).

authorities.name: URSIV
authorities.role: Government Office for Information Security - supervision

authorities.name: AKOS
authorities.role: Supervisor for electronic communications, media, digital services

authorities.name: SI-CERT
authorities.role: National CSIRT

fw: Security documentation (art. 21) and risk-management measures (art. 22) reference European and international standards; decrees pending to map obligations to ISO/IEC 27001.
Deadlines: 18 months after entry into force (19 Dec 2026); 12 months for entities already essential under the previous law (19 Jun 2026).
reg: Self-registration within 6 months (by 19 Dec 2025) via the URSIV online form; data includes MŠ ID, NACE code, security officer, public IP blocks, ASN, domain names.
inc: Until the dedicated platform ships (within 1 year), notifications by email to SI-CERT; voluntary reporting of cyber threats and near-misses possible.
aud: Random inspections for EE; IE inspected on evidence of breach; on-site, remote and security audits.
EE compliance assessment every 2 years; IE self-assessment every 2 years.
scope: Research institutions added (excluding education); general threshold ≥50 staff AND ≥€10M turnover/balance sheet except listed exceptions.
Public administration incl. national security/defence/law-enforcement entities (annex III) and urban municipalities; public entities face corrective orders, not fines.
other: DORA for finance; EU cybersecurity certification framework (Regulation 2019/881) integrated.
Logs kept ≥6 months (critical entities: on Slovenian territory); board approval of cyber programmes + training every 4 years; background checks allowed for sensitive positions.

timeline.text: ZInfV-1 adopted by the National Assembly (emergency procedure after EC formal notice)
Law enters into force
Self-registration deadline (6 months)

next: Government decrees mapping risk-management obligations to ISO/IEC 27001 expected; risk measures due 19 Jun / 19 Dec 2026.

countries.name: Estonia
countries.law: Cybersecurity Act amendment (Bill 739-SE), in force 1 Jan 2026
countries.fwName: E-ITS - ~1,600 measures in modules (BSI IT-Grundschutz + EVS-ISO/IEC 27001 based), updated every autumn
countries.summary: Law in force Jan 2026; registration due 1 Apr 2026 on eesti.ee; E-ITS framework; full compliance by Jan 2029.

authorities.name: RIA
authorities.role: Information System Authority - single point of contact, registry, incidents & crises

authorities.name: NCSC-EE
authorities.role: National Cybersecurity Centre - controls and audits

fw: Estonia meets NIS 2 minimums and details them via E-ITS: ~1,600 baseline measures grouped in modules (ISMS, OPS, INF, APP, SYS, DER…), each tagged basic/standard/high; entities apply the measures relevant to their assets.
E-ITS validation requires a dedicated audit - no automatic EE/IE split inside the framework; compliance with E-ITS also counts for referenced frameworks (e.g. German BSI certification).
Full compliance within 3 years (by 1 Jan 2029); §31 entities within 3 months; vital-service providers get 5 years from designation.
reg: Registration within 3 months of the law (by 1 Apr 2026) or of gaining EE/IE status, via eesti.ee with the RIA; changes within 2 weeks (3 months for digital services); non-EU digital providers appoint a representative.
Note: RIA withdrew its automated scope self-assessment tool early 2026, judged too complex to be reliable.
inc: First notification within 24h (except national-security entities), report within 72h, final report within 1 month; 'Raport' platform run by CERT-EE, simple email accepted.
aud: Annual security audits to verify effectiveness; no more than 12 months between two audits; targeted EE audits at entity cost (exceptions by decree); mutual evaluation possible, regular internal audit counts as independent review.
scope: Size thresholds clarified (≥50 staff + ≥€10M CA for IE; ≥250 staff + ≥€43M balance/€50M CA for some EE); R&D centres added; IS suppliers (IXP, MSP, MSSP, ITS) automatically EE regardless of size.
Public sector additions: public policy analysis centres, RMK (state forest), local authority associations.
other: Board member(s) formally responsible for approving security measures, with regular training; absent designation, the whole board is liable; info-sharing between entities regulated (RIA informed).

timeline.text: Bill 739-SE adopted by the Riigikogu
Law published in Riigi Teataja; in force 1 Jan 2026
Registration deadline on eesti.ee (3 months after entry into force)

next: During 2026: guidelines completing E-ITS; full compliance by 1 Jan 2029.

countries.name: Romania
countries.law: Emergency Ordinance OUG 155/2024 + Law 124/2025 + DNSC orders 1/2025 & 2/2025
countries.fwName: DNSC orders on cybersecurity measures; Belgian CyFun officially recognised - further orders pending
countries.summary: OUG in force Dec 2024; DNSC orders Aug 2025; recognises Belgian CyFun; annual maturity self-assessment; external audit 1 year after registration.

authorities.name: DNSC
authorities.role: National Cyber Security Directorate - regulator, CVD coordinator

fw: DNSC director issued two orders on cybersecurity measures; Romania joined the CyberFundamentals Scheme Owner Group (Oct 2024) and officially recognises Belgian CyFun.
Annual self-assessment of risk-management maturity submitted to the DNSC; EE remediation plan within 30 days of self-assessment, endorsed by management.
INFORB project (with Bulgarian MEG): practical guides for the food sector.
reg: Registration within 30 days of qualifying - effectively enforceable from 20 Aug 2025 (DNSC orders), so ~19/20 Sep 2025; DNSC identification decision within 60 days (EE) / 150 days (IE).
Interim offline tool (form emailed to the DNSC) until the NIS2@RO platform launches.
inc: Significant or cross-border incidents notified to the DNSC via the PNRISC platform; 24h warning, 72h initial notification, final report within 1 month.
aud: External compliance audit mandatory 1 year after registration, then every 2 years; results to the DNSC within 5 days; ad-hoc audits after major incidents or significant changes.
scope: CDN services, data-centre services and MSSPs explicitly included.
other: DNSC public 'Blacklist' platform of malicious domains; Romanian translation of the Belgian selection tool published Dec 2025.

timeline.text: OUG 155/2024 adopted and in force - founding text
Law 124/2025 approves and strengthens the OUG
DNSC orders 1/2025 (registration) and 2/2025 (risk methodology) in force
Belgian selection tool published in Romanian
Public consultation on risk management and board responsibilities

next: Additional regulations on risk-management measures and incident-reporting standards expected; sector authorities may specify details.

countries.name: Austria
countries.law: NISG 2026 (BGBl. 94/2025, published 23 Dec 2025) - in force 1 Oct 2026
countries.fwName: Implementing regulations per sector to be issued by the Cybersicherheitsbehörde
countries.summary: NISG 2026 adopted Dec 2025, applies from Oct 2026 (9-month transition); new federal cybersecurity authority; self-declaration by Jan 2028.

authorities.name: Bundesamt für Cybersicherheit
authorities.role: New federal cybersecurity authority (under BMI, organisationally independent) - competent authority, SPOC, national coordination

authorities.name: GovCERT
authorities.role: Public-administration CSIRT, interim national CSIRT

authorities.name: Austrian HealthCERT
authorities.role: Health-sector CSIRT

fw: Risk-management measures cover the 10 NIS 2 areas (risk analysis, incidents, continuity, supply chain, development, hygiene/training, cryptography, access control, MFA); sector implementing regulations pending.
EU sector rules (incl. DORA) take precedence where equivalent; CER definitions integrated; other recognised certifications may be considered.
reg: Registration within 3 months of entry into force (by 1 Jan 2027) via a secure electronic channel; changes within 2 weeks (3 months for seat address / EE-IE status).
inc: Online notification via 3 platforms (public administration, essential/digital services, energy); NIS 2 deadlines, except trust services: full report within 24h.
aud: Proactive supervision for EE (on-site/remote inspections, scans, ad-hoc audits); reactive for IE; mandatory self-declaration within 12 months of the registration obligation (by 1 Jan 2028).

On request: audit by accredited independent auditor (EE: 2 months to prove compliance; IE: 2 years); audit plan notified 1 month ahead; auditors accredited on qualifications (≥3 years, ≥20h/week) and exam.
From 1 Oct 2028 authorities may request proof of compliance via an independent auditor.
scope: ICT/DNS grouped as 'digital infrastructure' with requirements beyond NIS 2; health under GTelG 2012; research treated as an activity, not a sector.
Federal administration = EE regardless of size; Länder administration = IE; municipalities, education, courts, Parliament, national bank excluded.
other: Fines: EE up to €10M/2%, IE €7M/1.4%; registration/cooperation failures up to €50k (€100k repeat); temporary management bans with companies-register entry.

timeline.text: First bill (NISG 2024) rejected by the National Council
NISG 2026 bill presented by the government
NISG 2026 adopted (Nationalrat, then Bundesrat)
Published in the Federal Gazette (BGBl. 94/2025)
Official webinar on NISG 2026 and NIS 2

next: 1 Oct 2026: entry into force; 1 Jan 2027: registration deadline; 1 Jan 2028: self-declarations; 1 Oct 2028: auditor-backed proof requests possible.

countries.name: Bulgaria
countries.law: Cybersecurity Act amendment - adopted 5 Feb 2026, in force 17 Feb 2026
countries.fwName: Framework specifying technical & organisational requirements pending (≥3 ordinances to adopt)
countries.summary: Law finally in force Feb 2026 (16-month delay); framework and registration modalities still to be set by ordinance.

authorities.name: Ministry of e-Government
authorities.role: Supervision (with sector ministries: transport, energy, finance, health, water)

fw: At least 3 ordinances pending: minimum cybersecurity measures, telecom entities, national strategy - no technical framework formalised yet.
INFORB project with the Romanian DNSC provides practical guides for the food sector.
reg: The authority determines entity status and enters it in a dedicated registry, then notifies the entity; opt-out from the info-sharing registry possible on notification; changes within 2 weeks.
No registration platform or deadline published yet.
inc: Via form and platform to be specified in a dedicated regulation; NIS 2 deadlines (24h / 72h / 1 month) and report structure apply.
aud: Planned or unannounced inspections, on-site or remote; possible after security breaches or suspected illegality; self-assessment with report possible.
Control authorities also include the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Interior and State Agency for National Security (DANS).
scope: Sectors follow NIS 2 almost verbatim; food sector broader than annex II (any stage of production/processing/distribution).
Administrative entities (EA) form a third category besides EE and IE; scope automatic by sector and size, no threshold for telecoms, trust services, TLD registries, sole providers.
other: Restrictions on non-EU ICT products/services under discussion; CER, eIDAS and Cybersecurity Act referenced.

timeline.text: Cybersecurity law adopted at first reading by the National Assembly
EC reasoned opinion for failure to notify full transposition
Bill adopted at second reading
Law enters into force

next: First implementation deadlines; framework ordinance specifying technical and organisational requirements expected.

countries.name: Poland
countries.law: UC32 amendment to the National Cybersecurity System Act (signed 19 Feb 2026)
countries.fwName: No dedicated framework - ISMS required; PN-EN ISO/IEC 27001 & ISO 22301 recognised
countries.auditBody: National authority (Ministry of Digital Affairs + sectoral CERTs)
countries.summary: In force Apr 2026; ~42,000 entities in scope (incl. ~28,000 public); everything runs through the S46 platform; first EE audits by Apr 2028.

authorities.name: Ministry of Digital Affairs
authorities.role: Registry (Wykaz), large-scale incidents & crises; Government Plenipotentiary for coordination

authorities.name: Sectoral competent authorities
authorities.role: Supervision per sector

authorities.name: CSIRT MON / NASK / GOV
authorities.role: National CSIRTs + sectoral CSIRTs for incident reporting

fw: No national framework: entities implement an ISMS within 12 months; PN-EN ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 22301 designated as comparable standards.
Full compliance required by 3 Apr 2027 (12 months); compliance audit within 24 months.
High-risk vendor (HRV) mechanism: designated ICT suppliers must be phased out by regulated entities.
reg: Registration in the Wykaz registry via the S46 platform; entities already qualified on 3 Apr 2026 must self-assess and register by 3 Oct 2026; new entities within 6 months of meeting criteria.
Electronic application with qualified e-signature; changes within 14 days; authority can register entities ex officio.
inc: Alerts to the sectoral CSIRT via the dedicated S46 platform; NIS 2 deadlines and report content; public/banking entities notify under adapted rules.
Entities must adapt their IS to the platform's technical requirements within 6 months.
aud: EE: audits every 2 years (recurring every 36 months after first audit at 24 months); ex-ante + ex-post for EE, ex-post for IE; contest window 7 days.
Authority can require Polish translation of audit documents at the entity's cost; audits at entity's cost; first audits (and first possible fines) from 3 Apr 2028.
scope: Mining sub-sector and managed cybersecurity providers added to energy; nuclear energy added; more precise sub-sector definitions (e.g. research institutions).
Public entities split: EE (public finance sector, research institutes) and IE (local budget units, local cultural institutions); ~28,000 public bodies in scope.
other: DORA entities exempt from cyber rules and notifications; links with CER transposition and sectoral laws; fines up to €24M + daily penalties, payable within 14 days; 2 contact persons with vetted records; annual documented training for CEO and cyber officer.

timeline.text: Government approves the UC32 amendment transposing NIS 2
First reading in the Sejm; referred exclusively to the digital affairs committee
President Nawrocki signs the law (published 2 Mar 2026)
Law enters into force

next: 3 Oct 2026: self-assessment + S46 registration deadline; 3 Apr 2027: full compliance; 3 Apr 2028: first EE security audits.

countries.name: Cyprus
countries.law: Law N.60(I)/2025 amending the NIS law (in force 25 Apr 2025)
countries.fwName: Framework to be specified by the Digital Security Authority - publication expected
countries.incidentMethod: Online form or email to CSIRT-CY
countries.summary: Law in force Apr 2025; framework pending; notably strict timelines: 6h early warning, 15-day supplementary reports for long incidents.

authorities.name: DSA
authorities.role: Digital Security Authority (dsa.cy) - regulator with functional independence over public bodies

authorities.name: CSIRT-CY
authorities.role: National CSIRT - incident notifications

fw: The law carries the directive's security rules; the DSA may specify them and can require certified ICT products/services under EU cybersecurity certification schemes; national framework expected shortly.
reg: DSA draws up and maintains the EE/IE list (reviewed every 2 years); entities provide directive-required data once notified; changes within 2 weeks (3 months for DNS/TLD/cloud/data centres/social platforms).
Online self-assessment tool available to check eligibility.
inc: First notification within 6 hours of awareness (stricter than the 24h of the directive; 24h kept for trust service providers); initial assessment within 72h, final report within 1 month.
Incidents lasting over 1 month: progress reports every 15 days until the final report.
aud: Warnings, binding remediation instructions, cessation orders, publication of violations; ex-ante and ex-post for EE, ex-post for IE.
scope: Banking stays in scope for national strategy, large-scale incident cooperation and CSIRT assistance, but is not DSA-supervised (DORA).
Public bodies: certain enforcement measures (certification suspension, management liability) do not apply.
other: EU-CyCLONe participation enshrined; TLD/DNS databases must answer legitimate access requests within 72h; voluntary notifications accepted; active cyber-protection (network sensors) possible.

timeline.text: EC letter of formal notice for incomplete transposition
House of Representatives votes law N.60(I)/2025
Law enters into force
EC reasoned opinion despite entry into force (incomplete notification)

next: National cybersecurity framework publication expected shortly.

countries.name: Denmark
countries.law: NIS 2 Act (L 141 / LOV nr 434) + CER Act + sector laws (energy, telecom)
countries.fwName: Temporary framework 'Vejledning til NIS 2-loven' - 19 themes, 129 requirements (EE & IE)
countries.summary: Main law in force July 2025; temporary 19-theme guidance (ISO 27001 / IEC 62443 / NIST CSF); sector-based supervision.

authorities.name: Ministry of Resilience and Preparedness
authorities.role: Lead for the main act

authorities.name: SAMSIK
authorities.role: Sector authority for central government, municipalities, parts of manufacturing/chemicals; overall coordination

authorities.name: CFCS
authorities.role: Centre for Cyber Security - national CSIRT (within FE)

authorities.name: Named sector authorities
authorities.role: Digital, finance, energy, health, transport, maritime, water, food

fw: Temporary framework with 19 themes / 129 requirements applying to EE and IE alike, based on ISO 27001, IEC 62443 and NIST CSF; sector guides expected.
Local specificities: explicit Single-Point-of-Failure identification in risk analysis; OT continuity and detection adapted to operational constraints.
reg: EE/IE register within 2 weeks of falling in scope; digital service providers within 3 months; global registration deadline was 1 Oct 2025, via the national Virk platform.
inc: Reports submitted digitally via Virk.dk, automatically routed to competent authorities, CSIRT and SPOC; CFCS offers anonymised pre-notification consultations; declarations since 1 Jul 2025.
aud: Inspections in various forms (on-site or remote audits, document reviews) by sectoral authorities (energy agency, financial supervisory authority, health agency…).
scope: Central government units in scope by law; municipalities and regions as IE when acting commercially as public e-communications providers (>50 staff or >€10M).
Digital service providers in scope regardless of size.
other: Financial sector transposition explicitly aligned with DORA under Finanstilsynet; evaluation report to Parliament within 3 years; nis2.dk hub with sector checklists and guides.

timeline.text: Energy sector law (No. 258, NIS 2 + CER) in force
Parliament approves L 141 (NIS 2) and L 140 (CER)
CFCS publishes implementation guides incl. the temporary framework
Main law, CER law and telecom law in force
Global registration deadline on Virk

next: Sector-specific guides refining the measures expected; evaluation report within 3 years.

countries.name: Finland
countries.law: Cybersecurity Act (approved 11 Mar 2025, in force 8 Apr 2025)
countries.fwName: Traficom recommendation - 12 requirements mapped to ISO 27001, IEC 62443, NIST CSF/SP 800-53
countries.summary: Law in force Apr 2025; 12 requirements detailed by Traficom recommendation; registration fees; CER law since July 2025.

authorities.name: LVM
authorities.role: Ministry of Transport and Communications - transposition lead

authorities.name: Traficom / NCSC-FI
authorities.role: Single national contact point, national CSIRT

authorities.name: Sector authorities
authorities.role: Energy Authority, Tukes, Valvira, Fimea, Food Authority, ELY centre, FIN-FSA

fw: The law defines 12 requirements mirroring the directive; Traficom recommendations detail the associated measures, mapped to the EU directive, the act, ISO and NIST standards.
Risk-management model due within 3 months of entry into force (risk identification, procedures/responsibilities/objectives, protective measures).
reg: Registration within 1 month (May 2025) with the sector supervisory authority (multi-sector entities register with each); registration and annual maintenance fees apply.
Digital entities (DNS, marketplaces, cloud…) provide extended data.
inc: Significant incidents to the NCSC-FI CSIRT via the dedicated platform since 8 Apr 2025; 24h early warning, 72h report, final report 1 month later.
aud: Supervisory authority can inspect premises/IS and require a security audit after a serious incident or substantial negligence.
scope: Financial sector excluded (DORA); public sector handled via the public administration information management act.
Fines up to €10M or 2% of global turnover.
other: FISC published a national NIS 2 application guide; EC reasoned opinion 7 May 2025 (incomplete notification); CER law in force 1 Jul 2025.

timeline.text: Parliament definitively approves the Cybersecurity Act
Law in force; Traficom supervision recommendations published
Critical infrastructure protection & resilience law (CER) in force

next: Sector technical regulations possible from supervisory authorities.

countries.name: Sweden
countries.law: Cybersäkerhetslag SFS 2025:1506 (approved 10 Dec 2025, in force 15 Jan 2026)
countries.fwName: All-risk measures across the 10 directive areas - additional regulations expected
countries.summary: Law in force Jan 2026 (14-month delay); registration since Feb 2026; provisional IRON incident tool; sector + regional supervision.

authorities.name: MCF (Myndigheten för civilt försvar)
authorities.role: Single point of contact, cyber crisis authority, national CSIRT (CERT-SE)

authorities.name: Sectoral authorities
authorities.role: PTS, energy agency, Transportstyrelsen, Finansinspektionen, health and food agencies

authorities.name: 6 county administrative boards
authorities.role: Regional supervision (public administration, waste, research, some manufacturing)

fw: Technical, operational and organisational measures on an all-risk basis across the directive's 10 mandatory areas; no national framework published yet - additional regulations expected.
Lex specialis: Security Protection Act (SFS 2018:585) prevails where applicable; CER coordination - NIS 2 prevails unless CER is stricter.
reg: Registration as of 2 Feb 2026 via the MCF digital service; supervisory action possible if no notification within 14 days; changes within 14 days; self-assessment of eligibility (registry incl. self-classification EE/IE).
inc: MCF is central recipient, reports transmitted to CERT-SE; provisional IRON tool until the new reporting tool ships; 24h/72h/1-month deadlines.
'Significant' quantified: >€500k or 5% turnover loss, trade-secret exfiltration, death or serious health damage, disruptive unauthorised access (EU implementing regulation).
aud: EE: controls any time (regular audits, targeted audits, technical scans, premises access); IE: only on suspicion of non-compliance; no violation found → costs not charged.
scope: State authorities limited to those whose decisions affect cross-border mobility; regions, municipalities, municipal associations included; government, courts, Riksdag agencies excluded.
Fines payable within 30 days; uncollected after 5 years → cancelled; 40-year secrecy protection on incident-report information; Cybersäkerhetskollen maturity self-assessment tool.
other: DORA entities exempt from NIS 2 security/notification duties; IMY informed immediately if personal-data breach found during control.

timeline.text: Government submits the new cybersecurity law proposal
Riksdag approves 'en ny cybersäkerhetslag' (SFS 2025:1506)
Cybersecurity law and regulation in force
Registration opens (14-day duty)

next: Additional regulations (incl. MSB/MCF sector directives) expected.

countries.name: Luxembourg
countries.law: NIS 2 law promulgated 5 May 2026 (Mémorial A n°225) + CER law (n°226)
countries.fwName: No national framework yet - 10 minimum measures of art. 21 apply ('all-risks')
countries.summary: Law in force May 2026 (~19-month delay); ILR self-registration due 10 July 2026; SERIMA platform for incidents & risk assessments.

authorities.name: HCPN
authorities.role: High Commission for National Protection - transposition, cross-border cooperation, major crises

authorities.name: ILR
authorities.role: Institut Luxembourgeois de Régulation - supervisory authority

authorities.name: CSSF
authorities.role: Financial sector supervision

authorities.name: CIRCL
authorities.role: National CSIRT for private EE/IE - notifications, technical assistance, CVD

authorities.name: GOVCERT.lu
authorities.role: CSIRT for State administrations, public establishments, CER critical entities

fw: Pending a national framework (temporary or definitive), entities apply the 10 minimum measures of article 21; management bodies approve and supervise risk measures, with mandatory regular training.
ILR sector regulations already published: transport (12 Nov 2025) and energy (4 Feb 2026), with OT security focus.
reg: Self-registration on the ILR portal within 2 months of entry into force (by 10 Jul 2026); special-case digital providers had to register by 17 Jan 2025; annual updates and changes within 2 weeks; ILR reviews and confirms status; NIS 1 entities notified automatically.
inc: Notification via the centralised SERIMA portal (launched 2 May 2025 for NIS/CCEE/GDPR/CER); NIS 2 deadlines; risk assessments standardised with the MONARC method.
aud: Risk-based approach, no fixed frequency; full ILR controls expected from January 2027.
scope: CER-designated critical entities automatically EE regardless of size; public entities explicitly EE with dedicated CSIRT; defence/intelligence/army exempt.
National EE/IE list updated at least every 2 years; authority can prescribe specific ICT products/services/processes.
other: DORA entities exempt from equivalent provisions but still register with the ILR and notify non-DORA incidents; NIS 2 + GDPR notifications cumulative with anti-cumulation rule on fines.

timeline.text: Centralised incident portal launched on SERIMA
Registration deadline for special-case digital providers
Chamber of Deputies votes law 8364
NIS 2 and CER laws promulgated (Mémorial A n°225-226)
Law in force - NIS 1 law of 28 May 2019 repealed

next: 10 Jul 2026: EE/IE self-registration deadline; ILR regulations/circulars on notifications and technical requirements; national framework to adopt; full controls from Jan 2027; SERIMA training sessions.

countries.name: France
countries.law: 'Résilience' bill (transposes NIS 2, DORA, CER) - awaiting plenary examination
countries.fwName: ANSSI ReCyF 2.5 (17 Mar 2026, provisional) - 20 themes, 152 EE / 76 IE measures
countries.summary: Still not transposed - CJEU referral June 2026; ReCyF 2.5 provisional framework; plenary vote hoped for July 2026, ANSSI anticipates S2 2027.

authorities.name: ANSSI
authorities.role: National cybersecurity agency - framework, control and enforcement lead

fw: ReCyF 2.5 (17 Mar 2026): 20 themes across governance, protection, defence, resilience; 152 measures for EE, 76 for IE; framework comparison tool published.
An ephemeral 'NIS2+' variant was floated (excluding some sectors such as cosmetics distribution), shared with selected stakeholders only.
Presumption of conformity: ISO 27001 certification usable for certain measures; compliance evaluations expected annually internally, EE risk-analysis review every 3 years.
reg: Pre-registration open on the ANSSI website since 24 Nov 2025 (basic data; more expected in the final law); scope-check tool available (EE/IE classification).
inc: Incident notification expected to follow original NIS 2 timelines (24h / 72h / 1 month).
scope: Public administrations: local authorities >30,000 inhabitants, their management centres/fire services, State administrations, public industrial establishments, education/research establishments.
NIS 1 OSE automatically subject; software publishers under debate; OIV classification triggers automatic criticality uplift.
other: Bill aligns NIS 2, CER (REC) and DORA in a single 'Résilience' law.
reco: Confirm eligible entities with legal teams; pre-register with ANSSI; brief top management; consider early IS scoping and a gap analysis against the provisional ReCyF framework.

timeline.text: 'Résilience' bill presented in Council of Ministers, tabled in the Senate
Senate adopts the bill (61 committee amendments, 34 on NIS 2)
National Assembly special committee adopts 245 amendments
ANSSI opens its NIS 2 pre-registration platform
ReCyF 2.5 provisional framework published
European Commission refers France to the CJEU for non-transposition

next: Plenary examination in the July 2026 extraordinary session, enactment hoped summer 2026; ANSSI does not anticipate a permanent transposition before S2 2027.

countries.name: Netherlands
countries.law: Cyberbeveiligingswet (Cbw) - adopted by the Tweede Kamer, before the Senate
countries.fwName: Cbw (NIS2) Control Framework - 17 control domains, 26 measures, 5-level maturity model
countries.summary: Law targeted for 1 July 2026 (Senate pending); official control framework already published Sept 2025; ~8,000 entities in scope.

authorities.name: NCSC-NL
authorities.role: National Cyber Security Centre - implementation lead

authorities.name: Ministry of Justice and Security
authorities.role: Coordinating authority

authorities.name: Sector ministries
authorities.role: Supervisory authorities; sectoral CSIRTs for notifications

authorities.name: NOREA / ADR
authorities.role: IT auditors body & central government audit service - framework co-authors

fw: Cbw (NIS2) Control Framework (30 Sep 2025): 17 domains, 26 control measures, 5-category maturity model; not yet binding but expected reference for regulators.
Cbw sets the general frame; concrete rules come in sector ministerial regulations (6 ministries consulted drafts Nov-Dec 2025; education delayed).
Duty of care and 24h incident reporting apply immediately at entry into force; board members get a 2-year grace period to certify cybersecurity training.
reg: Voluntary registration open on mijn.ncsc.nl; obligation starts with the law; NCSC self-assessment, FAQ and preparation recommendations online.
inc: Multi-level system: notify the sectoral CSIRT AND the competent authority (supervising ministry); practical modalities (single platform vs sector portals) not yet confirmed.
aud: EE: ex-ante controls; IE: ex-post (on signals or incidents); no violation found → costs not charged to the entity.
scope: Higher education can be included by ministerial decree; municipalities, provinces and water boards included by default as EE - beyond the NIS 2 minimum.
other: Ministry of Interior published a mapping NIS 2 measures ↔ ISO 27002; ENISA compliance guide referenced; sector-specific EU acts prevail when equivalent.

timeline.text: NCSC publishes the Cbw (NIS2) Control Framework
Entry into force officially postponed to Q2 2026
Tweede Kamer (lower house) adopts the law
Eerste Kamer publishes its question report; Council of State opinion on the implementing decree

next: Entry into force targeted 1 Jul 2026 (possible slip to Q3); no transition period except governance training.

countries.name: Spain
countries.law: Cybersecurity Coordination and Governance bill - in parliamentary procedure
countries.fwName: CCN-STIC 892 (PCE-NIS2) withdrawn Mar 2025; updated ENS-based framework in preparation
countries.summary: Bill approved in Council of Ministers Jan 2025, still in Parliament; CJEU referral June 2026; ENS mapping as interim guidance.

authorities.name: CNC (planned)
authorities.role: Centro Nacional de Ciberseguridad - future single competent authority & SPOC (to be created within 12 months of the law)

authorities.name: CCN / OCC / Digital Transformation Ministry
authorities.role: Control authorities per sector and entity category

authorities.name: CCN-CERT / INCIBE-CERT / ESPDEF-CERT
authorities.role: Reference CSIRTs (public / private / defence)

fw: CCN-CERT published then withdrew the CCN-STIC 892 compliance profile (PCE-NIS2, ENS-based); an updated framework is in preparation; ENS updates by decree.
Management bodies responsible for risk measures with periodic training; EE must prove compliance via certification, IE may self-assess; ENS profile counts as compliance evidence (draft).
reg: Draft: self-assessment and submission of information to the control authority within 3 months of EE/IE status; changes within 2 weeks; CNC registry of digital providers planned; no platform yet.
inc: Notifications via the reference CSIRT on the Plataforma Nacional de Notificación y Seguimiento de Ciberincidentes (CCN-CERT run, 24/7); original NIS 2 deadlines.
aud: EE: ex-ante (on-site inspections, periodic audits by ENS-accredited certification bodies); IE: ex-post on evidence.
other: DORA financial entities explicitly excluded from risk/notification/supervision provisions; equivalent EU regulations prevail.

timeline.text: Bill approved by the Council of Ministers (urgent procedure)
CCN-CERT withdraws CCN-STIC 892 v1; updated framework in progress
EC reasoned opinion for failure to notify transposition
European Commission refers Spain to the CJEU (with France)

next: Adoption by Parliament and publication in the BOE; new CCN-STIC 892; CNC created by royal decree within 12 months of entry into force.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.law: Cyber Security and Resilience Bill - before the House of Lords (not an EU transposition: updates the NIS Regulations 2018)
countries.fwName: Codes of Practice to be issued by the Secretary of State (admissible as compliance evidence)
countries.summary: CS&R Bill in the Lords since June 2026; Royal Assent expected late 2026, full implementation through 2028; two-tier penalty regime.

authorities.name: DSIT
authorities.role: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology - policy lead

authorities.name: NCSC
authorities.role: National Cyber Security Centre

authorities.name: 12 sector regulators + ICO
authorities.role: Competent authorities; ICO registers digital & managed service providers

fw: Seven reform pillars: MSPs in scope, two-tier criticality oversight (ex-ante/ex-post), strengthened incident reporting, full cost recovery, decree-based updates, delegated scope extension, 'critical dependency' designations.
Secretary of State may issue Codes of Practice - breach is not an offence but admissible as evidence of (non-)compliance.
reg: RDSP/RMSP must register with the ICO within 3 months of section 14 commencement; non-UK entities appoint a local representative; ICO shares registries with GCHQ/NCSC every 12 months; data-centre OES register within 3 months of designation; changes within 7 days.
inc: Initial alert within 24h, full notification within 72h (OES, RDSP, RMSP); expanded impact criteria; third-party-caused incidents must reference the origin entity.
aud: Designated authorities and appointed inspectors: premises entry, document seizure, interviews, security testing; Statement of Strategic Priorities aligns supervision with national security.
scope: Data centres (1 MW / 10 MW thresholds), managed service providers, load controllers ≥300 MW, specific digital services; authorities can designate Critical Suppliers.
Applies to Crown data-centre services with security-service exceptions.
other: Penalties: up to £10M/2% standard, £17M/4% serious, £100k/day continuing; mandatory ransomware-payment reporting under separate consideration.

timeline.text: CS&R Bill first reading, House of Commons
Committee stage completed; amended version published 25 Feb
Report stage and third reading - Commons approve the bill
First reading in the House of Lords

next: Full Lords sequence then Royal Assent expected late 2026; phased commencement, full implementation expected through 2028.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.law: National Cyber Security Bill - General Scheme Aug 2024, before the Oireachtas since early 2026
countries.fwName: NCSC Risk Management Measures (16 RMMs, non-binding guidance); CyFun co-ownership, ISO 27001 & NIST CSF accepted
countries.regTool: 'Am I in Scope?' tool; portal targeted July 2026
countries.summary: Bill still in the Oireachtas; 16 RMMs published as compliance floor; 8 sectoral authorities pre-designated; registration portal targeted July 2026.

authorities.name: NCSC (IE)
authorities.role: Lead competent authority, national CSIRT, single point of contact

authorities.name: 8 sectoral NCAs
authorities.role: CRU (energy/water), ComReg (digital), Central Bank, IAA, CRR, Transport, NTA, Health agency

fw: 65-page RMM guidance (24 Jun 2025): 16 risk-management measures, non-binding today, compliance floor upon enactment.
Ireland co-owns the Belgian CyFun framework and is moving to ratify it as national certification scheme; ISO 27001 and NIST CSF 2.0 also accepted; SME-friendly national scheme in development.
reg: Registration portal targeted for July 2026 with 3-month self-registration window (conditional on enactment); entities will register with their sectoral authority; 'Am I in Scope?' tool online.
Minimum data: contact details, NACE code, CRO number, sector, member states served.
inc: Early warning to NCSC/CSIRT-IE within 24h, notification with initial assessment within 72h, final report within 1 month (per public drafts).
aud: EE: proactive supervision (regular audits, on-site/off-site inspections, scans); IE: reactive; temporary suspension of EE activities possible on non-compliance.
scope: Named EE public bodies: Government Ministers, CSO, C&AG, Revenue, OPW, NSSO; all other public bodies default to IE.
other: NCSC powers beyond NIS 2 (proactive scanning, consent-based sensors, DNS blocking) contested on fundamental-rights grounds; DORA lex specialis with Central Bank as NIS 2 NCA for finance; EC reasoned opinion May 2025.

countries.name: Norway
countries.law: Digital Security Act (NIS 1) in force 1 Oct 2025; unified NIS 2 + CER bill being finalised
countries.fwName: Digital Security Regulation (NIS 1 requirements); NSM Fundamental Principles recommended meanwhile
countries.incidentMethod: Reports to sector authority, copy to NSM
countries.summary: EEA country: NIS 1 regime live since Oct 2025; NIS 2 incorporation planned during 2026, no new official date after slippage.

authorities.name: Ministry of Justice and Public Security
authorities.role: Legislative lead

authorities.name: NSM
authorities.role: National Security Authority - guidance (Veileder), default supervisor

authorities.name: Sectoral authorities
authorities.role: Supervision (e.g. NVE for energy)

fw: Current regime = NIS 1 via the Digital Security Act and its regulation: all-risk approach, proportionate measures, management personally responsible (art. 20), specific measures list (art. 21).
Government recommends applying NSM's Fundamental Principles of Cybersecurity while awaiting NIS 2.
reg: Essential service providers self-identify 'without delay' to the NSM and the competent sector authority.
inc: Reports to the sectoral supervisory authority with copy to NSM (national contact point).
scope: Energy already heavily regulated by NVE (IKT-forskrift) easing transition; NIS 2 scope will add rail, port, airport infrastructure via sector regulations.
other: National Security Act (Sikkerhetsloven) prevails on national-security conflicts; certified ICT products can be required (CSA); NSM guides on nsm.no.
